# Validation rules

- **Schema version:** 1.0.0
- **Model:** One-dimensional damped mass–spring oscillator — `m x″ + c x′ + k x = 0`
- **Solver method:** Classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta (RK4), fixed step, state (x, v)
- **Canonical units:** SI (kg, N/m, N·s/m, m, m/s, s). Only the declared unit set is normalised.

Every issue carries `path`, `rule_id`, `severity`, `kind`, `message` and `guidance`. `kind` decides the disposition: `clarify` → ask the user; `reject` → refuse without calling the solver; `warn` → informational; `output` → output check.

| Rule ID | Kind | Severity | Meaning | Corrective guidance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `REQUIRED_MISSING` | clarify | error | Required field missing | Supply the missing value with a unit, or confirm the documented default. |
| `UNIT_MISSING` | clarify | error | Value has no unit | Add a unit from the allowed set for this field. |
| `UNIT_UNKNOWN` | clarify | error | Unit not recognised | Use one of the allowed units or convert the value yourself. |
| `UNIT_MISMATCH` | clarify | error | Unit has the wrong dimension | Use a unit of the right physical dimension for this field. |
| `TYPE_INVALID` | reject | error | Wrong type | Send a JSON number for value and a string for unit; booleans and numeric strings are not accepted. |
| `VALUE_NOT_FINITE` | reject | error | Value is NaN or infinite | Provide a finite number. |
| `RANGE_MIN` | reject | error | Below minimum | Use a value at or above the minimum. |
| `RANGE_MAX` | reject | error | Above maximum | Use a value at or below the maximum. |
| `MODEL_UNKNOWN` | reject | error | Unsupported model | Only the approved model damped_spring can run. |
| `FIELD_UNKNOWN` | reject | error | Unknown field | Remove fields that are not part of the schema. |
| `CROSS_STEP_CAP` | reject | error | Too many integration steps | Increase dt or shorten the duration so duration/dt does not exceed the step cap. |
| `CROSS_DT_EXCEEDS_DURATION` | reject | error | Step larger than duration | Choose dt no larger than the duration. |
| `CROSS_STABILITY` | reject | error | Step outside RK4 stability region | Reduce dt (or stiffness/damping) so that the fastest rate times dt stays below the reject threshold. |
| `STABILITY_WARN` | warn | warning | Step coarse for the fastest dynamics | Accuracy may be poor; reduce dt and check convergence. |
| `OUTPUT_NONFINITE` | output | error | Non-finite output | Reduce dt or check settings. |
| `OUTPUT_LENGTH` | output | error | Unexpected output length | Internal consistency failure; report it. |
| `OUTPUT_GRID` | output | error | Time grid not uniform/monotonic | Internal consistency failure; report it. |
| `OUTPUT_ENERGY` | output | error | Energy grew beyond tolerance | Reduce dt; a dissipative system must not gain energy beyond numerical tolerance. |
| `OUTPUT_REFERENCE` | output | warning | Deviates from analytic reference | Reduce dt and compare convergence; treat the result as low accuracy. |

## Example messages

- `settings.mass: required field is missing.`
- `settings.duration: supply s; “5” has no unit.`
- `settings.dt: 0.2 s exceeds maximum 0.05 s.`
- `settings: 500,000 integration steps exceeds cap of 200,000.`
- `result.displacement: non-finite value at index 34.`

## Assumptions

- Linear spring and linear viscous damping; no driving force.
- Point mass in one dimension; no friction other than viscous damping.
- Double-precision floating point; results are deterministic for identical validated settings on the same Python build.
- Bounds are engineering and resource limits, not physical laws.

## Limits

- Not fusion research and not production scientific software; an educational workflow demo.
- Accuracy degrades as the largest characteristic rate times dt grows; see the stability rules.
- Energy check allows a 0.1 % tolerance above the initial energy; it does not claim exact monotonic decay.

Step rule: n = ceil(duration / dt); the effective step is duration / n (never larger than dt); n + 1 samples are returned.
Reference: Closed-form analytic solution (underdamped, critical, overdamped, undamped) used for the output reference check.
